thread_analysis.thread_summary: JVC Kenwood (contact Suganuma) consults Allion (Itsuo Sakai, with Masaya Iida and Toshitaka Mochizuki copied) about whether describing a device registered as 'BR/EDR/LE' 'Class 1' using narrower terms ('BR/EDR', 'Class 2') in marketing and manual materials would violate Bluetooth SIG rules.
all_questions_found: Is it a rule violation to describe a BR/EDR/LE Class 1-registered device as 'BR/EDR' 'Class 2' in marketing/manual materials? (see thread_0251_case_01)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: LE detectability depends on whether an Advertising-packet-emitting UI feature is actually implemented, independent of registration scope; Class 1 and Class 2 output power ranges overlap between 0 and 4dBm, allowing a 'Class 2 equivalent' description when actual output is managed within that range.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Marketing/manual description questions that seem like simple compliance checks can have nuanced, defensible answers grounded in actual functional implementation (UI features) or official overlapping technical ranges (output power classes) rather than requiring an exact match between registration scope and product description language.
